It has not been cooked or tested by this project, has had no professional food-safety review and is not publication-ready. Times and temperatures are starting points. Air fryers differ; check the food and follow your appliance manual and any product cooking instructions.
summary: Sweet potato wedges cooked until the edges colour and the inside softens. About half an hour is a planning estimate; thickness, basket space and any extra batch change the total.

ingredients.item: Sweet potato, scrubbed and left unpeeled
ingredients.note: Ordinary potatoes can use the same method; allow about 5 minutes longer for a firmer, crisper surface.
Ground cumin, or any supermarket chip seasoning, does the job just as well.
Optional; helps form a crisp coating.

method.instruction: Cut each sweet potato in half lengthways, then into wedges about 2 cm thick along the outside edge, and toss them with the oil, the cornflour and the seasoning.
Set the air fryer to 200°C, preheating only if your appliance manual says to.
Lay the wedges in one layer, skin down where you can. Crowding traps steam and softens the surface. If they will not fit in a single layer, cook them in two batches.

Cook for 18 to 22 minutes, turning at about 10 minutes. A fork entering easily and coloured edges are texture cues; thick wedges may need another 3 or 4 minutes. These cues do not override product preparation instructions, especially for frozen substitutes.

Sweet potato sugars may stick to the metal. After cooking, switch off, unplug and let the appliance cool before cleaning. Follow its manual for removable parts, soaking and cleaning products; never immerse the electrical unit or assume water alone is enough.

yield_note: Serves two as a side. About 30 minutes in total for one batch; extra batches take additional cooking and handling time. Editorial measuring convention for these original notes: tablespoon 20 mL; teaspoon 5 mL. These are volume measures, not gram conversions.
provenance_note: Original practical notes written for this repository, with no outside source cited. Quantities suit a small household batch in a domestic air fryer and have not been checked in a test kitchen.

caveats: Do not treat all vegetables as automatically safe without cooking controls. Wash and prepare fresh sweet potatoes appropriately; follow packet cooking and storage instructions for packaged or frozen substitutes, which may require thorough cooking.
Sweet potato is sugary and scorches faster than it looks. If your machine runs hot, check at 15 minutes and turn them earlier when the edges start to darken.
Hot sugar sticks to skin. Tip the wedges out of the basket rather than picking them out by hand.
These are practical notes, untested by this project and never given a professional food-safety review.
